messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: argument "burnin" is missing, with no default
parts:
Jorge

There is a default burnin, it just isnt explicit in the function help page. If you run the example from the cfa function (without the parallel argument so we can see the advance of the iterations), you see the default adapt, burnin, and sample iterations. By default does 100 adapt, 4000 burnin, and 10000 samples

> library(blavaan)
Loading required package: runjags
Loading required package: lavaan
This is lavaan 0.6-1.1141
lavaan is BETA software! Please report any bugs.
This is blavaan 0.2-5.214
blavaan is more BETA than lavaan!
> HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
+               textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
+               speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
> 
> fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)
Loading required namespace: rjags
Compiling rjags model...
Calling the simulation using the rjags method...
Adapting the model for 1000 iterations...
  |++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++| 100%
Burning in the model for 4000 iterations...
  |**************************************************| 100%
Running the model for 10000 iterations...
  |**************************************************| 100%
Simulation complete
Calculating summary statistics...
Note: The monitored variables 'lambda[1,1,1]', 'lambda[4,2,1]', 'lambda[7,3,1]', 'alpha[1,1,1]', 'alpha[2,1,1]' and 'alpha[3,1,1]' appear to be
non-stochastic; they will not be included in the convergence diagnostic
Calculating the Gelman-Rubin statistic for 36 variables....
Finished running the simulation
Computing posterior predictives...
> summary(fit)
blavaan (0.2-5.214) results of 10000 samples after 5000 adapt+burnin iterations

messages.subject: Re: argument "burnin" is missing, with no default
parts:
There is also a bug in at least one version, where you have to explicitly add the arguments 

burnin=4000, sample=10000

to your command. Or you could change the numbers if you want.

messages.subject: Re: argument "burnin" is missing, with no default
parts:
On a perhaps somewhat related note, I came across the following error:

y <- rnorm(100)
y <- as.data.frame(y)
model <- '#Intercept
    y ~ 1 

#variance
y ~~ y
'
n.samples <- 1000
fit.model <- blavaan(model, data=y, n.chains = 4, burnin = 1000, sample = n.samples, adapt=1000)
Error in mc$sample * n.chains : non-numeric argument to binary operator

This error does not occur in the development version so it is probably also solved, but I thought I'd post it just to be sure. In the development version this works just fine.
